adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:97 — unsubscribe is a bare GET with real side effects and default Rails GET requests skip CSRF token verification, so a cross-site `` on any page can silently mute a logged-in user's topic notifications without consent

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates state (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) and is wired up via GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Because it’s a GET endpoint with real side effects, it is susceptible to CSRF-style triggering (e.g., an ``), since Rails’ CSRF protections generally target non-GET requests. The diff also explicitly exempts the action from `check_xhr` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`), making it easier to hit from non-XHR contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for this topic (e.g. never visited/tracked it), so `tu.notification_level` on the next line raises NoMethodError instead of handling the unsubscribe gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without any nil-guard. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic (e.g., user never visited/tracked the topic before clicking the unsubscribe link), `tu` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, breaking the unsubscribe flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe action reimplements the notification_level toggle logic (regular/muted) that already lives in TopicUser.change, leaking model logic into the controller and duplicating business rules

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the controller manually toggles `tu.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted` based on `> :regular`. However, the diff shows `TopicUser.change` only applies whatever `attrs[:notification_level]` is provided (and publishes MessageBus updates); it does not contain the same “toggle regular/muted” business rule. So the claim that the controller is duplicating toggle logic that already lives in `TopicUser.change` is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe` action mutates TopicUser.notification_level via a plain GET request with no CSRF/verification token, so any cross-site link/image/embed can silently unsubscribe a logged-in victim from a topic (GET-based CSRF, only current session auth, no proof the link was opened from the actual recipient's email)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topics#unsubscribe` action and exposes it via `get` routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" ...`). In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, it mutates server state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` based solely on the user’s session (`current_user.id`), with no CSRF token or other one-time verification shown. Because it’s a GET endpoint and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe`, a cross-site request (e.g., an `` or link) could trigger the notification-level change for a logged-in user. This is a concrete, diff-grounded GET-based CSRF/state-change issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:103 — TopicUser.find_by(...)` result `tu` is not nil-checked before calling `tu.notification_level`, so a logged-in user who was never subscribed to the topic (no TopicUser row) hits a NoMethodError/500 (denial of service via crafted unsubscribe link)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without checking whether `tu` is nil. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, this will raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:193 — New `unsubscribe` controller action has zero spec coverage (no request/controller spec exists for TopicsController#unsubscribe).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new nontrivial `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (toggles `TopicUser.notification_level`, redirects on slug mismatch, and renders via `perform_show_response`), but the only spec change shown is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` for `unsubscribe_url`; the diff does not add any request/controller spec covering the new controller behavior. However, the claim that *no* such spec exists anywhere in the repo cannot be fully verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:193 — No test distinguishing json vs html format behavior for unsubscribe (e.g., blank slug redirect skipped for json requests per `!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial branching behavior in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` via `if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` (i.e., redirect for HTML when slug is blank, but not for JSON). The diff also adds both slug and no-slug routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). No tests are added for this controller behavior (the only spec change is in `email/message_builder_spec.rb`), so there is indeed no coverage distinguishing JSON vs HTML behavior for the new unsubscribe endpoint.
